title: Adaptive epoch-based kernel affinity and deterministic rollback for heterogeneous multi-stream decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see intermittent correctness regressions and non-deterministic stalls when heterogeneous decode streams (mixed sequence lengths, quantization levels, and batch affinities) trigger fast CUDA Graph captures and variant kernel selection. Root cause analysis points to non-deterministic kernel binding heuristics that change between capture and replay when stream composition shifts mid-epoch, and to incomplete quiescing of streaming prefill epochs leading to partial KV states on rollback.

Goal: Introduce an epoch-based kernel affinity profile and a rollback-safe graph commit protocol that: (1) deterministically pins kernel variants for the duration of an epoch, (2) snapshots minimal stream runtime state at commit points, and (3) enables fast, correct rollback/replay when stream membership or sequence length distributions change. The approach should reduce capture/replay correctness incidents and lower tail latency variance without materially increasing average latency.

Proposed design:
- Epoch model: group concurrent requests into short-lived "epochs" (configurable, defaults: 250ms) during which kernel affinity profiles are stable. An epoch boundary triggers computation of an affinity profile based on observed sequence-length histogram, quantization flags, and occupancy signals.
- Kernel affinity profile: a compact descriptor (list of kernel choices + confidence scores) derived by the kernel selector. Profiles are namespaced by model-version + device-topology + quantization-tag. Profiles are deterministic for a given epoch input distribution.
- Commit and snapshot: when a CUDA Graph capture is about to be committed for an epoch, the runtime writes a small snapshot (fence token, KV-root-hash, epoch-id, affinity-profile-id) to an ephemeral metadata store on the device. This allows replay to verify that the runtime state matches expectations and fail fast into a safe fallback if mismatched.
- Rollback-safe replay: on replay, if snapshot verification fails (epoch mismatch, KV-root-hash difference), the runtime will: (a) abort the captured graph replay, (b) transparently fallback to a safe single-stream decode path for affected requests, and (c) schedule a deterministic re-capture only after the epoch boundary and with an updated affinity profile.
- Fast recovery heuristics: implement lightweight incremental re-capture where only affected kernel segments (attention or matmul kernels) are re-bound using previously cached kernels to reduce warmup cost.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests that exercise epoch boundary conditions and forced snapshot mismatches.
- End-to-end harness replay fuzz tests show 0 incorrect completions across 100k mixed-stream replay attempts.
- P50/P95 tail-latency impact <= 5% compared to baseline on our internal benchmark for chat workloads; P99 regressions must be investigated and justified.
- Production rollout gated behind canary with runtime-1.21 feature-flag, with automated rollback if correctness or error-rate thresholds tripped.

Risks and mitigations:
- Increased capture latency due to profiling at epoch boundaries: mitigate by sampling (only profile subset) and caching affinity profiles keyed by a compact signature.
- Snapshot metadata contention in dense GPU pools: use per-device ephemeral allocation and garbage collect stale epoch entries after N seconds.
- Edge cases where fallback path is slower and causes SLO violation: bundle a fast single-stream decode optimization and prioritize fallback for low-latency tiers only.

Testing plan:
- Expand fuzz harness to generate stream-interleaving schedules and assert deterministic outputs under repeated capture/replay.
- Add synthetic long-tail experiments with mixed quantization to measure warmup cost of incremental re-capture.
- Canary pool: deploy behind runtime-1.21, route 5% of traffic per-region to the feature-flagged machines and monitor decode correctness, error-rate, and tail latency for 72 hours.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature-gated implementation into main with thorough unit tests (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3247).
2) Internal QA + fuzzing for 1 week.
3) Canary (5% traffic) for 72 hours.
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% if metrics stable and no correctness regressions.

Monitoring / Observability:
- New runtime metrics: epoch_count, affinity_profile_hits, snapshot_verify_failures, incremental_recapture_latency_ms.
- Dashboards: per-model epoch stability heatmap and snapshot failure alarms.
- Alert: snapshot_verify_failures > 5/min sustained -> auto-disable feature-flag and page on-call.

2025-02-25 - Marcus Li: Implemented prototype of epoch-id + snapshot metadata on device. Verified we can write/read small fence tokens without host-side roundtrips. PR opened for initial infra: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3247.

2025-02-27 - QA (Sofia Martinez): Added fuzz cases to the replayer harness. Observed 13 failures out of 10k runs with current naive re-capture; failures clustered when quantization flags flipped mid-epoch. Next: add profile invalidation on quantization delta.

2025-03-01 - Marcus Li: Implemented profile namespacing by quantization-tag and added incremental recapture for attention kernel segments. Local benchmark: 12% warmup improvement versus full recapture on mixed quant workloads.

2025-03-03 - PM (Lena Novak): Reviewed rollout plan and canary thresholds. Agreed to 72h canary at 5%/region and automatic rollback if snapshot_verify_failures exceed 1% of requests or error-rate increases by 0.5% absolute.
